words.prose: {{ar:مَٰلِكِ}} ({{tr:māliki}}) opens the ayah as a genitive continuation of the prior praise chain, not as a detached title. Its construct shape points forward to the specific Day, while definiteness travels back from the final term through the chain. The accepted reading field keeps kingly sovereignty and intensified possession nearby, but the aligned surface gives the reader a possessor with disposal over time and reckoning. Its rare divine-ownership field places ownership of the Day beside ownership of dominion (3:26), while inside the Fatiha it pivots the opening from mercy into accountability and prepares the direct worship and guidance requests (1:5; 1:6).

words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمِ}} ({{tr:yawmi}}) is the middle hinge of the chain: governed by the Owner and governing the reckoning term. Its article-less construct form becomes definite through what follows, so the reader receives a named Day rather than an indefinite date. The root can name ordinary days, open spans, and event-days, but here the recurring reckoning formula (51:12; 70:26; 82:17; 82:18; 83:11) narrows that elasticity into the decisive eschatological time. Variant case evidence shows how much depends on the genitive: the Day remains a possessed construct term, not merely an adverbial backdrop. It turns the praise sequence toward direct worship and path outcome (1:5; 1:7), and its sound binds forward so the temporal noun and the reckoning noun land as one audible formula.

Its definiteness reaches backward through the construct, making the whole phrase point to the known reckoning order. The local formula selects judgment and recompense, but the root pressure keeps debt-settlement, obligation, obedience, and submission in the reader's ear; the Day is not just a verdict date but the settlement of a binding moral order. The final word completes the recurring Day formula (15:35; 26:82; 37:20; 38:78; 51:12; 56:56; 70:26; 74:46; 82:15; 82:17; 82:18; 83:11), while its wider order field can be heard beside upright-order references (9:36; 12:40; 30:30; 98:5) without displacing the local reckoning sense. reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Ownership of reckoning as custody of the whole account.** Lexical evidence: م ل ك B002, ownership and disposal; د ي ن B002, reckoning and recompense; ن ع م B001 in 1:7, bestowed favor; غ ض ب B001 in 1:7, anger toward retaliation. Structural cue: the ayah sits before the worship/help pledge and before the sorting of favored, angered, and astray. Assigned role: مالك holds the account in which favor and liability are settled. Abductive move: the packet supplies ownership, recompense, favor, and wrath; I infer an accounting mechanism whose final disposal belongs to the owner. Reading change: the Day of dīn reads as custodial settlement, not only a scene of sovereignty.

2. **Dīn as obedience now and recompense later.** Lexical evidence: د ي ن B001, obedience/submission/law; د ي ن B002, reckoning/recompense; ع ب د B003 in 1:5, worship and submissive obedience. Structural cue: “Day of dīn” is immediately followed by “You we worship.” Assigned role: dīn links the present act of submission to a later order of reckoning. Abductive move: the packet supplies the adjacency; I infer a temporal arrow from present obedience to future accounting. Reading change: the ayah reads not as an isolated eschatological line but as the horizon under which 1:5 becomes intelligible.

3. **Debt and favor as an unsettled economy of dependence.** Lexical evidence: د ي ن B003, financial debt/credit; ن ع م B001, benefaction given to another; ع و ن B001 in 1:5, seeking help. Structural cue: the speaker asks for help and later names people upon whom favor was bestowed. Assigned role: dīn’s debt branch makes favor and help feel like obligations that cannot be self-settled. Abductive move: the packet supplies debt, help, and favor; I infer that dependence creates an account held by the مالك. Reading change: “Day of dīn” also reads as the day when received aid and favor are accounted for.

4. **Malik as mainstay and center of the path-order.** Lexical evidence: م ل ك B005, mainstay of a matter; م ل ك B006, center/main course of road or valley; ص ر ط B001 in 1:6–1:7, straight road; ق و م B009 in 1:6, support/mainstay. Structural cue: the path appears after this ayah, and “straight” is built from standing/support. Assigned role: مالك becomes the central controlling support that keeps the road-order from scattering. Abductive move: the packet supplies road/center/mainstay; I infer that judgment is the axis around which the requested path is stabilized. Reading change: the ayah reads as the structural center of the surah’s movement, not only as a title of rule.

5. **The “day” as severe event rather than mere date.** Lexical evidence: ي و م B003, event-day or severe occasion; غ ض ب B001 in 1:7, intensified anger toward retaliation; ض ل ل B002/B003, disappearance/loss. Structural cue: the day is defined by dīn and later by contrasted destinies. Assigned role: يوم marks the crisis-time when hidden loss and provoked anger become manifest. Abductive move: the packet supplies severe occasion and later moral outcomes; I infer that the “day” is an event of exposure and sorting. Reading change: the ayah reads as an occurrence of decisive manifestation, not merely a calendrical period.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 1:6’s path language unexpectedly activated م ل ك B006, the main course of road or valley. That made مالك less exclusively regal and more axial: the Owner of the Day also owns the centerline by which movement and judgment are held together.
reader_a.turkish_prose_synthesis_md: “Din gününün sahibi” ifadesi, hesabın tamamını elinde tutan malik anlamına gelir. Din burada hem şimdi yaşanan itaat ve kulluk düzenini, hem de ilerideki hesap ve karşılığı taşır. Nimet, yardım ve borç çağrışımlarıyla bu ayet, alınan lütufların ve yönelişlerin hesabının kime ait olduğunu gösterir. Yol imgeleri geri dönünce Malik, sadece kral değil, yolu ve hesabı ayakta tutan merkez eksen gibi de okunur.

reader_b.activated_readings_md:
1. **The severe event-day of reckoning under dominion.** Evidence: `م ل ك B003` kingship/dominion, `ي و م B003` event-day or severe occasion, and `د ي ن B002` reckoning/recompense. Mechanism: the three roots lock into a forensic-sovereign scene: dominion specifies who controls the event, يوم gives the occasion weight, and دين supplies accounting. The packet supplies these three elements; I infer their convergence into a tribunal-like mechanism. Abductive move: when “day” is paired with recompense rather than ordinary sequence, it becomes an event of settlement. Reading change: the ayah reads as ownership of the decisive occasion, not only ownership on a calendar day.

2. **The path has a controlling center and main course.** Evidence: `م ل ك B006` center/main course of road or valley, activated by `ص ر ط B001` road/path in 1:6–1:7; `ق و م B008` straightness/uprightness; `ه د ي B001` showing the road. Mechanism: later ṣirāṭ turns ملك from sheer possession toward the “main course” that governs where one can travel. The packet supplies road, straightness, guidance, and the road-center branch; I infer that ملك can function as the central channel of the path. Abductive move: a path becomes safe when its governing center is known and not confused with side routes. Reading change: “مالك” also activates as the holder of the road’s central line, so judgment is connected to navigation.

3. **Debt, favor, and repayment.** Evidence: `د ي ن B003` debt/credit, `ن ع م B001` bestowed favor in 1:7, `ح م د B001` thanksgiving in 1:2, and `ع و ن B001` help in 1:5. Mechanism: favor and help create received benefit; دين as debt/recompense turns the day into a reckoning of dependence. The packet supplies favor, help, thanksgiving, and debt; I infer an economy of received bounty and answerability. Abductive move: one who receives نعمة and عون stands in a relation that must be acknowledged rather than possessed as private merit. Reading change: the ayah can read as the day when benefaction, gratitude, obligation, and recompense are brought into one account.

4. **Standing before the owner.** Evidence: `ق و م B013` resurrection and people standing before their Lord, activated by `ق و م` in “المستقيم” at 1:6; `ر ب ب B001` lordship; `د ي ن B002` reckoning. Mechanism: the later straight-standing root carries a resurrection branch backward into يوم الدين: the path of uprightness anticipates standing before the Lord. The packet supplies the standing/resurrection branch and the reckoning frame; I infer temporal reversal from future standing back to present path. Abductive move: a straight path matters because it trains or leads to the final standing. Reading change: “يوم الدين” is not only an external future event; it presses backward into present posture.
reader_b.retrospective_surprises_md: 1:6–1:7 changed this ayah most: the later صراط made `م ل ك B006` visible, so ملك was no longer only royal possession but also the center or main channel of a road. 1:7’s نعمة also made `د ي ن B003` debt/credit unexpectedly relevant: the day of דין can account for received favor, not only punish wrongdoing.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A dependent community turns toward a sovereign divine addressee through worship, service, obedience, and petition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The devotional relation extends lexically from willing worship into ownership and coercive service, while lordship also carries the countervailing function of nurture.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Worship and Obedient Submission
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Worshippers direct humble obedience to the one recognized as deity and organizing religious authority.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: worship as an act `ء ل ه:B001/m01`; the worshipped deity `ء ل ه:B001/m02`; obedient religious submission `د ي ن:B001/m01`; humble worship and service `ع ب د:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The scene joins the divine object of worship to the human act of worship, then specifies the relation as obedience enacted with humility. Religion is active here as an ordering relation rather than merely a named doctrine.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A dependent community turns toward a sovereign divine addressee through worship, service, obedience, and petition.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Sovereignty, Ownership, and Service
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A lord and king possesses a domain, governs it, and stands over dependents whose service ranges from honored attendance to enslavement.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: divine lordship `ر ب ب:B001/m01`; proprietary mastery `ر ب ب:B001/m02`; kingship and sovereignty `م ل ك:B003/m01`; ownership and disposal of property `م ل ك:B002/m01`; the enslaved dependent `ع ب د:B001/m01`; coercive dominion `د ي ن:B004/m01`; the honored or venerated servant `ع ب د:B006/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Lordship and kingship supply the governing agent, ownership supplies the legal relation to a domain, and servitude supplies the dependent role. The honored servant and the enslaved subject expose opposite social realizations of the same vertical relation.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Good is conferred through compassion and maintenance, stabilized as welfare, and answered by praise or recognition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Tenderness expands into practical provisioning, repair, guardianship, and structural support, while praise can function either as gratitude or as a claim imposed by a patron.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Patronage, Support, and Claimed Recognition
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A patron supplies aid and the mainstay of another's life, then may present that support as a favor deserving praise.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: aid and mutual support `ع و ن:B001/m01`; the mainstay of an affair `م ل ك:B005/m01`; structural and livelihood support `ق و م:B009/m01`; benefaction or favor `ن ع م:B001/m02`; blessing as a conferred good `ر ب ب:B016/m03`; seeking praise for a favor `ح م د:B005/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Aid, mainstay, and livelihood form one support mechanism. The social relation becomes patronage when the giver converts that material dependence into a demand for acknowledgment.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Names, utterances, reputation, and bearing make identity or commitment socially legible.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The naming and address field reaches from divine invocation into assent, grammatical qualification, poetic exchange, and the ceremonial presence of a reputed captain.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Assent, Certification, and Qualification
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: An utterance confirms a claim, delegates judgment, or narrows it through difference, exception, negation, and approximation.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: affirmative response `ن ع م:B004/m01`; certification or delegated judgment `د ي ن:B007/m01`; otherness and difference `غ ي ر:B005/m01`; exception and negation `غ ي ر:B005/m02`; the approximating or quantifying particle `ر ب ب:B015/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Assent commits the speaker, certification authorizes another's word or judgment, and qualification sets the limits of the commitment. Approximation and exception show that discourse governs not only truth but also scope.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: marriage contract `م ل ك:B004/m01`; bride conveyed to her husband `ه د ي:B006/m01`; kinship relation `ر ح م:B002/m01`; affectionate gift `ه د ي:B004/m01`

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Domestic and wild animals gather into recognizable herds, are classified and led, and can fall outside the group as ownerless strays.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: wild-cattle herd `ر ب ب:B014/m01`; herd of wild donkeys `ع و ن:B006/m01`; livestock wealth `ن ع م:B005/m01`; middle-aged animal `ع و ن:B002/m01`; leading animal followed by the herd `م ل ك:B008/m01`; ownerless stray `ض ل ل:B005/m01`
